notes: GenApp's VSAM 'update policy' (LGUPVS01, LINKed by LGUPDB01): the key and WF-POLICY-DATA built as in LGAPVS01, then EXEC CICS READ FILE('KSDSPOLY') INTO(WS-FileIn) LENGTH(WS-Commarea-Len = EIBCALEN) RIDFLD(WF-Policy-Key) KEYLENGTH(21) UPDATE and REWRITE FROM(WF-Policy-Info) LENGTH(64); on NORMAL it GOBACKs. Each scenario's KSDSPOLY is compared after the task. Every non-NORMAL RESP in this program goes to WRITE-ERROR-MESSAGE, whose first act is EXEC CICS LINK PROGRAM('LGSTSQ') (GenApp's TS/TD error logger, defined in the CSD); the equivalence harness runs one program and has no port of LGSTSQ, so a scenario that reaches it is refused (Unsupported: LINK PROGRAM(LGSTSQ)). The error paths -- NOTFND on the READ ('81', ABEND LGV3) and a failing REWRITE ('82', ABEND LGV4) -- are therefore NOT exercised here; they need LGSTSQ modelled (or ported) first. The READ's LENGTH (EIBCALEN) is not modelled by the stub; record 64 bytes, INTO 1024, so no LENGERR either way. Keys: WF-POLICY-KEY is the request-type byte followed by 20 digits, so every key mixes a letter and digits; the WHEN OTHER scenario puts a digit in that first byte (digits sort before letters in ASCII, after them in EBCDIC). No browse is issued, so no key order is exercised (the comparison sorts each side's records by key bytes). Data: ksdspoly.txt is built from GenApp's own sample policies (base/cntl/db2cre.jcl's policy rows joined with their endowment / house / motor / commercial rows), laid out as WF-POLICY-INFO (request-type letter + customer + policy number, then the type's 43 bytes) -- the record LGAPVS01 writes; policy 7 (type C, no commercial row) is left out. ONE synthetic record is added: key '9' + customer 6 + policy 7 with blank data, so that the WHEN OTHER branch has an existing record to rewrite (GenApp never writes such a key itself).
